title: Compatibility exception workflow and staged rollout for legacy model variants
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Summary: Several enterprise customers (finance and healthcare) have requested that we allow temporary compatibility exceptions for legacy model variants that are otherwise scheduled for deprecation or re-quantization. The ask is to create a gated, auditable workflow that supports: (a) granting short-term version pins with contract-backed SLAs, (b) staged rollout for new variants that preserves traffic split and easy rollback, and (c) explicit eval gates that capture quality/regression signals before full promotion.

Background: Historically our catalog deprecation + pinning flows assume customers upgrade to the newest vetted variant on a fixed cadence. Enterprise buyers often require exception lanes due to internal validation cycles, regulatory approvals, or long lead integrations. Without a formalized path we see ad-hoc pins, operational toil for ops/eng, and silent technical debt.

This ticket scopes the PM playbook, the UI/Console affordances, and the acceptance criteria needed for Eng to implement a rights-managed temporary pin + staged rollout process integrated with the eval gating service and audit logs.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Console exposes a 'Request Compatibility Exception' flow that captures reason, requested duration (max 90 days), contract reference, and required approver.
AC-2: Requests route to a configurable approver group and create an audit entry with immutable metadata (requester, approver, timestamps, justification).
AC-3: On approval, the system creates a temporary pin for the legacy variant with automatic expiration and a linked rollback policy.
AC-4: The staged rollout mechanic supports defining percent-based traffic slices (0-100) over time windows and supports automatic pause/rollback on eval-gate regressions.
AC-5: Eval gates run a defined prompt set and produce a regression score; if regression > configured threshold, traffic automatically pauses and notifies stakeholders.
AC-6: All actions generate system notifications and a single-line change history visible on the model variant page.
AC-7: Integration tests cover approval flow, pin creation/expiration, staged rollout progression, and eval-gate-triggered rollback.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Design): Finalize form fields, approver groups, and expiration semantics — owner PM. (Week 1)
Phase 1 (Backend): Implement temporary pin API, audit log entries, and expiration worker; expose endpoints for staged rollout control. (Weeks 2-3)
Phase 2 (Eval): Add hook to eval service to run regression checks during staged rollout slices; configurable thresholds per request. (Week 3)
Phase 3 (Console): UI for request creation, approver dashboard, and variant timeline visualization. (Week 4)
Phase 4 (Pilot): Run with 2 enterprise customers in beta lane, monitor signals and adjust thresholds. (Week 5-6)
Phase 5 (GA): Open to all enterprise tenants and include in runbook and docs. (Week 8)
Fallback: Manual revoke for emergency deprecations and immediate rollback endpoint for ops.
decision_log: 2026-03-11 - Decided to cap temporary pins at 90 days by default to balance customer needs and catalog hygiene (PM + Legal).
2026-03-12 - Chose to implement percent-based staged rollouts rather than only time-based promotions to enable safer canaries (Eng + SRE).
2026-03-13 - Eval gate outputs will be stored as immutable artifacts linked to audit entries for compliance and post-mortem.
2026-03-14 - Default eval threshold set to regression <= 3% relative to baseline for first pilot; will tune with customer signals.
risks: Risk: Extensions of temporary pins in absence of good guardrails could increase support load and catalog fragmentation.
Risk: Misconfigured eval thresholds may cause false-positive rollbacks disrupting customer traffic during pilot.
Risk: Approver group delays could extend support SLAs and frustrate customers expecting faster pin grants.
Mitigation: Automatic reminders to approvers, clear expiry enforcement, and aggregated reporting on outstanding exceptions.
stakeholders: SRE: On-call rotation for rollback endpoint
Solutions Eng: pilot coordination with customers
